security_audit.summary: All 102 static matches are false positives caused by Markdown command examples, fixed project-relative paths, and standard Prisma environment configuration. The reviewed files are documentation only; no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or embedded executable payload was found. Some documented Prisma commands can modify or delete database data, so users should review targets and confirmations before running them.

remediation.issue: Destructive database commands are documented alongside routine commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add prominent warnings and target-environment checks before examples using migrate reset, db push --force-reset, or --accept-data-loss.

remediation.issue: Examples load database connection settings from environment files.
remediation.suggestion: State that .env files must remain uncommitted and that production credentials should use the deployment secret manager.

remediation.issue: Static scanning misclassifies Markdown backticks and relative generator paths.
remediation.suggestion: Consider scanner rules that distinguish fenced documentation examples and fixed generated-output paths from executable code.

content.value_statement: Prisma CLI workflows can affect schemas, generated clients, and database data. This skill provides command guidance, safety boundaries, and references for each Prisma CLI task.
actual_capabilities: Explains Prisma project initialization and datasource setup.
Guides Prisma Client generation, including watch mode and generator selection.
Describes schema introspection, schema push, seeding, and raw SQL execution.
Provides development and production migration command guidance.
Covers schema validation, formatting, debugging, Studio, and MCP commands.
limitations: It provides guidance and does not run commands or inspect a live database.
It does not replace database backups, access controls, or change review.
It does not cover Prisma Compute deployment workflows.
Command availability can vary by Prisma version and database provider.

use_cases.title: Start a Prisma project
use_cases.description: Set up a project, choose a datasource provider, and prepare configuration files.

use_cases.title: Plan a safe schema change
use_cases.description: Choose between development migrations, production deployment, or a local schema push.

use_cases.title: Operate migration automation
use_cases.description: Use production migration guidance and protect database credentials in CI workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me initialize a Prisma project for PostgreSQL. List the files created and the environment variables I must configure.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a client
prompt_templates.prompt: My Prisma schema changed. Explain how to validate it and regenerate Prisma Client without changing database data.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a schema workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare prisma db push and prisma migrate dev for a local development change. Include data-loss and collaboration considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production checklist for prisma migrate deploy in CI. Include secret handling, backups, migration review, and rollback planning.

output_examples.input: I changed my Prisma schema during local development. What should I do next?
output: Validate and format the schema first.
Choose migrate dev when the change needs a tracked migration.
Regenerate Prisma Client after the schema workflow completes.
Confirm the selected database is a local development target before applying changes.

output_examples.input: Can I use prisma db push in production?
output: Use tracked migrations for production changes when possible.
db push does not create migration history and can cause data loss.
Review schema changes and use a backup before any destructive operation.

best_practices: Confirm the database URL and environment before every state-changing command.
Use tracked migrations and reviewed CI deployment steps for production databases.
Run validation and regenerate Prisma Client after relevant schema changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run reset, force-reset, or accept-data-loss commands against an unverified database.
Do not commit .env files or database credentials to source control.
Do not use db push as a substitute for reviewed production migration history.

faq.question: Does this skill run Prisma commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance and references only.

faq.question: When should I use prisma migrate dev?
faq.answer: Use it during development when you need a tracked migration from schema changes.

faq.question: When should I use prisma migrate deploy?
faq.answer: Use it in production automation to apply pending reviewed migrations.

faq.question: Is prisma db push safe for production?
faq.answer: It is usually better for prototyping or local development because it does not create migration history.

faq.question: How should I handle DATABASE_URL?
faq.answer: Keep it in local environment files or a deployment secret manager, and never commit secrets.

faq.question: Does this include Prisma Compute deployment?
faq.answer: No. Use the separate prisma-compute skill for Prisma Compute deployment workflows.
